definition: Fortuitous means happening by chance rather than design, often with a lucky result.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fortuitous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fortuitous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A fortuitous wrong turn led the hikers straight to the waterfall they had given up on finding.
An unplanned event simply was not arranged, while a fortuitous one adds a stroke of luck to the accident.
A fortuitous encounter is a lucky accident, but a miraculous one seems to defy the odds entirely, as if chance alone could not explain it.

Accidental means happening by chance, not on purpose, and it is neutral or even negative — an accidental fire, an accidental deletion. Fortuitous keeps the accident but adds a welcome result: the wrong turn that finds the waterfall. An accidental discovery might be a disaster; a fortuitous one is a gift.

Chance, used before a noun (a chance meeting, a chance remark), simply marks something as unarranged — it takes no side on whether the outcome was good. Fortuitous usually smiles: it describes the lucky accident, the one you would never undo. Any encounter can be a chance encounter; only the welcome ones read as fortuitous.

Sailors spoke of good fortune when the winds favored them, using the same Latin root for chance, fors, that gives fortuitous its meaning.

A college student left her sketchbook on a city bus.
The stranger who found it happened to be an art director at a children's publisher, and she flipped through the drawings while waiting for her stop.
Two weeks later the student, who had planned none of it, signed her first illustration contract.
The whole career began with one fortuitous mistake.
The lucky outcome came entirely from an unplanned accident, which is what fortuitous means.

Fortuitous describes something that happens by accident, usually a welcome accident (a fortuitous discovery, a fortuitous meeting).

Keep it distinct from propitious: fortuitous looks backward at a lucky accident that already occurred, while propitious looks forward, describing signs and conditions that favor what is about to happen.

In 1928, Alexander Fleming returned from vacation to find mold growing in one of his petri dishes.
Most researchers would have washed the dish and started over.
Fleming noticed instead that no bacteria grew in a ring around the invader.
The contamination was fortuitous: an airborne spore he never invited had drifted onto exactly the right plate, and the accident pointed him toward penicillin.
Historians still argue about how much was luck, but the drug that followed saved millions of lives.
